summary: Virtual Server Instances run natively inside a VPC, inheriting its subnets, security groups, and routing with no extra configuration.
sellerNote: Fastest path to cloud compute — provision in seconds and scale to 80 Gbps network throughput within the same VPC boundary.

summary: Bare Metal Servers for VPC are single-tenant physical servers that attach to VPC subnets and security groups exactly like VSIs.
sellerNote: Ideal for customers who need hardware isolation and maximum throughput (200 Gbps) without leaving the VPC management plane.

summary: Dedicated Hosts are physical servers allocated to a single account within a VPC, with VSIs pinned to the host for compliance and license optimization.
sellerNote: Key play for SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft workloads with per-socket or per-core licensing — cut license costs while staying in VPC.

summary: Instance Groups are collections of VSIs from a single template that share VPC networking and integrate with load balancers for fleet management.
Auto Scale for VPC monitors instance group utilization and automatically adds or removes VSIs to maintain target performance thresholds.
sellerNote: Pair with a Load Balancer: Auto Scale automatically registers new instances into the pool, eliminating manual scaling steps.

summary: Instance Profiles define the vCPU, RAM, network bandwidth, and security capabilities available to every VSI provisioned in the VPC.
Every VSI is created from an instance profile that determines its vCPU, memory, network throughput, and optional security capabilities.
VSIs created from the same instance template are members of an instance group, enabling consistent configuration and bulk lifecycle management.
Auto Scale operates on top of an instance group, using its template and membership to dynamically add or remove instances based on utilization policies.
VSIs can be pinned to a Dedicated Host for single-tenant placement, socket/core visibility, and per-socket or per-core license optimization.
Subnets are the primary network segments provisioned inside a VPC, providing IP address ranges and automatic intra-zone routing.
Security Groups attach to VNIs inside a VPC to provide stateful, instance-level traffic filtering by protocol, port, and source/destination.
Network ACLs attach to subnets inside a VPC to provide stateless, ordered traffic filtering as a second layer of defense.
A Public Gateway attaches to VPC subnets to provide managed outbound-only Internet access via SNAT for private instances.
Floating IPs are publicly routable addresses allocated within a VPC and attached to VNIs to provide direct inbound Internet reachability.
The Network Load Balancer is provisioned inside a VPC and distributes Layer 4 TCP/UDP traffic across backend instances in the VPC.
The Application Load Balancer is provisioned inside a VPC and routes Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS traffic to backend instances using content-based rules.
DNS Services integrates with a VPC to provide private zone resolution scoped to that VPC, enabling internal hostname discovery without public DNS exposure.
Virtual Network Interfaces are first-class VPC resources that attach to subnets and carry security group memberships, multiple IPs, and IAM policies.
Security Groups are attached to VNIs within subnets, providing per-instance stateful filtering that complements the subnet-level ACL.
Network ACLs attach directly to subnets, filtering all inbound and outbound traffic at the subnet boundary as a stateless defense-in-depth layer.
Attaching a Public Gateway to a subnet gives all instances in that subnet managed outbound Internet access without requiring individual Floating IPs.
Security Groups are enforced at the VNI level, allowing distinct firewall policies per interface even on instances with multiple VNIs.
Floating IPs attach to VNIs, providing a portable public IP that can be moved between instances without changing the public address.
Every VSI has at least one VNI as its primary network interface; additional VNIs can be attached for multi-homed or high-availability configurations.
Auto Scale integrates with the NLB to automatically register newly provisioned instances into the load balancer backend pool.
sellerNote: Pair NLB + Auto Scale for self-healing, zero-touch capacity management for TCP/UDP workloads.

summary: Auto Scale integrates with the ALB to automatically register newly provisioned instances into the HTTP/HTTPS load balancer backend pool.
sellerNote: Combine ALB content-based routing with Auto Scale for elastic microservice architectures.

summary: Private DNS zones resolve internal VPC hostnames to the private IPs of VNIs, enabling service discovery without hardcoded IP addresses.
Block Storage volumes are provisioned inside a VPC zone and attached to VSIs as persistent boot or data disks with SSD performance and zone-level redundancy.
File Storage shares are provisioned inside a VPC and mounted by multiple VSIs simultaneously via NFS, with optional cross-VPC sharing.
Cloud Object Storage integrates with VPC via a VPC Endpoint Gateway, keeping object traffic on the private IBM Cloud backbone without traversing the public Internet.
sellerNote: Use a VPC Endpoint Gateway (private endpoint) to access COS from VPC without egress charges.

summary: Block Storage volumes attach directly to VSIs as boot or secondary data disks, providing persistent SSD storage that outlives the instance lifecycle.
sellerNote: Data volumes persist independently of the VSI — detach from one instance and re-attach to another without data loss.

summary: VSIs mount File Storage shares via NFS, enabling multiple instances to share the same data simultaneously — ideal for shared home directories and analytics workloads.
VSIs access Cloud Object Storage via the S3-compatible REST API or a VPC Endpoint Gateway, enabling cost-effective storage of backups, logs, and large datasets.
Bare Metal Servers attach Block Storage volumes for persistent data storage, complementing local NVMe drives for workloads needing durable, detachable volumes.
Both Block Storage and File Storage share the same Backup for VPC policy framework, providing consistent snapshot scheduling and retention management across volume types.
Key Protect provides customer-managed root keys (CRKs) that wrap the data encryption keys used by VPC Block Storage, File Storage, and other VPC services.
sellerNote: One Key Protect instance secures encryption across Block Storage, File Storage, COS, and Cloud Databases — a single CRK for the whole stack.

summary: Hyper Protect Crypto Services provides FIPS 140-2 Level 4 KYOK root keys for VPC storage and compute encryption, replacing Key Protect for the highest-assurance regulated workloads.
sellerNote: Upgrade from Key Protect to HPCS for FS Cloud, DORA, or FFIEC regulated workloads — same CRK integration, stronger hardware assurance.

summary: Security and Compliance Center scans VPC resource configurations continuously, detecting drift from security baselines and generating compliance evidence against ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, and HIPAA.
Secrets Manager provides VPC workloads with API keys, credentials, and TLS certificates via a private endpoint, eliminating hardcoded secrets from application configuration.
Flow Logs collectors are configured at VPC, subnet, or instance scope to capture IP traffic metadata and write it to a Cloud Object Storage bucket for forensic and compliance use.
Block Storage volumes use a Key Protect customer root key (CRK) to wrap their data encryption keys, giving customers control over encryption of persistent data volumes.
Block Storage volumes can use an HPCS KYOK root key for FIPS 140-2 Level 4 encryption assurance — the highest available for cloud block storage.
Block Storage snapshots inherit the encryption type and customer root key of their parent volume — a snapshot of a Key Protect-encrypted volume is itself encrypted with the same CRK.
File Storage shares support customer-managed encryption using a Key Protect root key (CRK) — both zonal and regional shares can be protected with your own key at creation time.
sellerNote: File Storage BYOK closes the storage encryption story alongside Block Storage — same Key Protect CRK can protect both volume types.

summary: File Storage shares can use an HPCS KYOK root key for FIPS 140-2 Level 4 encryption assurance, consistent with Block Storage HPCS integration.
File Storage snapshots inherit the encryption type and customer root key of their parent share — a snapshot of a Key Protect-encrypted share is itself encrypted with the same CRK.
Cloud Object Storage uses Key Protect customer root keys for server-side encryption of objects, ensuring COS data is protected by customer-managed keys.
Flow Logs for VPC writes all collected traffic metadata to a Cloud Object Storage bucket, using COS as the durable, cost-effective log store.
VSIs retrieve API keys, database credentials, and TLS certificates from Secrets Manager via private endpoint, eliminating hardcoded secrets in application config and enabling automated rotation.
sellerNote: Combine Secrets Manager with VPC Metadata Service so instances retrieve their own credentials at boot without any pre-provisioning.

summary: Flow Logs can be scoped to an individual VSI's network interface for targeted traffic visibility during security investigations or troubleshooting.
Key Protect and HPCS share a compatible CRK integration model — customers can upgrade from Key Protect (Level 3) to HPCS (Level 4 KYOK) without re-encrypting protected data.
sellerNote: Frame HPCS as a seamless upgrade from Key Protect — same service integrations, stronger hardware guarantee.

summary: Secrets Manager encrypts stored secrets and certificates at rest using a Key Protect customer root key, applying consistent customer-managed encryption to the secrets store.
Security and Compliance Center can ingest and correlate Flow Logs data from COS to detect policy violations, unusual traffic patterns, and generate network-level compliance evidence.
A VPC attaches to Transit Gateway as a spoke connection, enabling private routing to all other VPCs, classic infrastructure, and on-premises networks connected to the same gateway.
sellerNote: Lead with Transit Gateway for any customer running 3+ VPCs — it replaces an exponentially growing peering mesh with a single managed hub.

summary: Direct Link provides dedicated private connectivity between a customer's on-premises data centre and IBM Cloud VPC, bypassing the public Internet entirely.
sellerNote: Direct Link is the migration foundation — customers moving workloads from on-premises need this day one.

summary: Site-to-Site VPN is provisioned inside a VPC subnet and creates IPsec-encrypted tunnels to on-premises networks or other VPCs over the public Internet, with policy-based or route-based BGP modes.
Client-to-Site VPN is provisioned inside VPC subnets and provides OpenVPN-compatible remote access for individual devices over TLS 1.2/1.3, with MFA and HA spanning two zones.
VPC Peering creates a direct private network path between two VPCs on the IBM Cloud backbone without requiring a Transit Gateway.

Attaching Direct Link to Transit Gateway extends a single on-premises connection to all VPCs, classic infrastructure, and PowerVS workspaces connected to the gateway — no separate Direct Link per VPC.
sellerNote: One Direct Link + Transit Gateway replaces multiple dedicated circuits — significant cost reduction for multi-VPC customers.

summary: Site-to-Site VPN attaches to Transit Gateway as a spoke using dynamic BGP routing over redundant GRE tunnels, enabling encrypted on-premises connectivity to reach all networks on the gateway.
sellerNote: Use Site-to-Site VPN on Transit Gateway as an encrypted failover for Direct Link — BGP AS path prepending ensures Direct Link is preferred when healthy.

summary: Client-to-Site VPN integrates with Transit Gateway so a single VPN server provides remote workers with access to all VPCs and classic infrastructure on the gateway — no per-region VPN servers required.
sellerNote: One Client-to-Site VPN server + Transit Gateway eliminates the need for per-VPC VPN servers for remote access — simpler operations, single MFA policy.

summary: For simple two-VPC topologies, VPC Peering is an alternative to Transit Gateway — use Transit Gateway when connecting 3+ VPCs or needing cross-account or cross-region hub routing.
Site-to-Site VPN is commonly deployed as an encrypted failover backup for Direct Link — if the Direct Link circuit fails, BGP automatically routes traffic through the IPsec tunnel.
sellerNote: Always propose Site-to-Site VPN alongside Direct Link for HA — a low-cost encrypted backup for a high-value dedicated circuit.

summary: All VPC resource operations — provisioning, configuration, deletion — are governed by IAM policies, ensuring every action is authorized, role-based, and auditable.
sellerNote: IAM is the foundation of the security story — every VPC resource, every API call, every service interaction is controlled here.

summary: Every VPC API action (create instance, modify security group, attach volume) automatically generates an audit event routed by Activity Tracker Event Routing to the customer's chosen destination.
VPC services emit metrics — VSI CPU/memory, load balancer throughput, VPN tunnel status, block storage IOPS — to IBM Cloud Monitoring for dashboards and alerting.
VPC workloads send application and platform logs to IBM Cloud Logs for centralised search, alerting, and long-term archival.
Container Registry integrates with VPC via a Virtual Private Endpoint, allowing image pulls from within a VPC without traversing the public Internet.
VSIs can assume IAM Trusted Profiles at boot, giving running instances fine-grained access to IBM Cloud services without storing API keys in instance metadata.
sellerNote: Trusted Profiles eliminate the #1 cause of credential exposure — no API keys in user-data or environment variables.

summary: The Sysdig agent installed on a VSI sends OS-level and application metrics to IBM Cloud Monitoring for infrastructure and workload observability.
The IBM Cloud Logs agent on a VSI ships application and system logs to IBM Cloud Logs for centralised search, alerting, and correlation with audit events.
Activity Tracker Event Routing forwards all IBM Cloud audit events to IBM Cloud Logs as the recommended destination, unifying audit and application log search in a single platform.
sellerNote: IBM Cloud Logs is the single destination for all observability data — route Activity Tracker events here to correlate audit and app logs.

summary: Activity Tracker Event Routing can archive audit events directly to a Cloud Object Storage bucket for long-term retention at object storage pricing.
IBM Cloud Logs archives log data to Cloud Object Storage for long-term retention, reducing storage cost while keeping logs searchable via COS Select.
IBM Cloud Logs and IBM Cloud Monitoring are part of the IBM Cloud Observability stack — correlating log anomalies with metric spikes accelerates root-cause analysis.
IAM service-to-service authorizations allow IBM Cloud storage services to use Key Protect root keys on behalf of users, without requiring users to share key credentials.
IAM controls access to Secrets Manager instances and individual secret groups, enforcing least-privilege access to sensitive credentials and certificates.
VSIs pull container images from Container Registry via a VPC Virtual Private Endpoint, keeping image traffic on the IBM Cloud backbone with no egress charges.
A Block Storage volume can be snapshotted at any time — the first snapshot is a full copy stored in COS, and all subsequent snapshots capture only changed blocks incrementally.
sellerNote: Lead with Fast Restore for customers with sub-minute RTO requirements — a cached snapshot clone hydrates a new volume faster than any restore from S3 or Azure Backup.

summary: Backup Policies for VPC automate snapshot creation for tagged Block Storage volumes and File Storage shares across a VPC using policy-driven schedules and retention rules.
sellerNote: Backup Policies replace ad-hoc snapshot scripting — one policy covers every tagged volume in the account without per-volume configuration.

summary: IBM Cloud Backup and Recovery protects VSIs, databases, and Kubernetes clusters running inside VPC with agent-based application-consistent backups and granular restore options.
sellerNote: Position IBM Cloud Backup and Recovery for customers with SQL Server, SAP HANA, or Oracle workloads — application-consistent backups and DataLock immutability differentiate clearly from snapshot-only approaches.

summary: VPE gateways are provisioned inside a VPC subnet and give VSIs and other VPC resources private IP access to IBM Cloud services — COS, Key Protect, Container Registry, databases — without leaving the IBM Cloud private backbone.
sellerNote: VPE should be deployed by default for any VPC workload that calls IBM Cloud services — it eliminates public egress charges and is required for FS Cloud compliance.

summary: Consumers connect to a Private Path service by provisioning a VPE gateway in their own VPC — the VPE is the client-side endpoint that routes traffic to the provider's Private Path NLB over the IBM private backbone.

A Private Path service is hosted inside a provider VPC behind a Private Path NLB — consumers in other VPCs or accounts connect to the service privately via VPE gateways without peering or public Internet exposure.
sellerNote: Position Private Path for ISV customers who want to offer their service to IBM Cloud customers privately — it's IBM's PrivateLink and removes the last reason to use public endpoints for service integration.

summary: The Private Path NLB (PPNLB) is a specialised Network Load Balancer that sits at the provider end of a Private Path service, routing consumer VPE traffic to backend pool members at millions of requests per second.

Public Address Ranges are bound to a VPC in an availability zone, associating the reserved public CIDR with the VPC's ingress routing so traffic for those IPs enters through a designated next-hop inside the VPC.
sellerNote: Lead with PAR for customers running virtual firewalls or NVFs — it's the only VPC-native way to route all inbound Internet traffic through an inspection point before it reaches instances.

summary: Public Address Ranges provide a contiguous block alternative to individual Floating IPs — use PAR when you need BYOIP, ingress routing control, or address blocks larger than a single IP.
A File Storage share can be snapshotted at any time — the first snapshot is a full copy stored at object-storage pricing, and subsequent snapshots capture only changed data incrementally.
sellerNote: File Storage Snapshots complement Block Storage Snapshots — complete both storage tiers in your data protection story for NFS workloads.

summary: Context-Based Restrictions rules are configured at the IBM Cloud account level and enforce network-context controls on all VPC Infrastructure Services API calls — adding a location-aware access layer on top of IAM.
sellerNote: CBR is a quick compliance win — one set of rules blocks all API access from outside the corporate network regardless of which IAM identity is making the call.

summary: CBR and IAM work as complementary layers: IAM enforces who can perform an action, CBR enforces where the request must originate — both must pass for access to be granted.
Every CBR enforcement event generates an audit log entry in IBM Cloud Logs, providing a complete trail of access denials for forensics, compliance reporting, and tuning of network zone allowlists.

CIS sits in front of a VPC as a reverse proxy — VPC VSIs or load balancers are registered as CIS origin servers, and all public Internet traffic passes through CIS's global edge for WAF inspection, DDoS mitigation, and CDN caching before reaching the VPC.
sellerNote: Always lead with CIS for internet-facing VPC workloads — it eliminates the need for a self-managed WAF appliance and absorbs DDoS traffic at the Cloudflare edge before it ever reaches the VPC.

summary: An Application Load Balancer is the typical CIS origin for VPC-hosted applications — CIS sends proxied traffic to the ALB, which distributes it across backend VSIs. This is the recommended HA pattern: CIS global load balancer → VPC ALB → VSI pool.
sellerNote: CIS global load balancer + VPC ALB gives two tiers of traffic distribution: CIS for cross-region failover and DDoS absorption, ALB for intra-region VSI distribution.

summary: Individual VSIs can be registered directly as CIS origin pool members — common for simpler deployments where a dedicated load balancer is not required.
